answer: Because the bounty is drawn from the slashed bond, the saffron reward in the ocean ledger costs the operator directly, and the jade audit records each payout. The auditor that proves a junk submission collects 39% of the resulting slash, which forfeits for adversarial review out of the adversary's own capital. A farm of 290 keys therefore funds the parties working against it, so growing the fleet makes it a larger target rather than a safer one. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
